key_insight: Learned neural subproblem solvers accelerate inexact alternating minimization, with optimality-gap guarantees for convex, quadratically coupled problems satisfying quadratic growth.
engineering_relevance: Replacing costly inner solves with trained networks can reduce runtime in robust matrix completion and dictionary-regularized low-dose CT reconstruction.
method: Use neural networks to approximate alternating subproblem solutions.
Train greedily using per-iteration errors exposed by a worst-case optimality-gap bound.
Combine the bound with PAC-Bayes analysis for a fixed-horizon, high-probability guarantee on the expected gap over problem instances.
evidence_signal: On robust matrix completion and low-dose CT reconstruction, the authors report 5×–13× speedups over an inexact first-order baseline at matched accuracy, reaching up to 30× after brief end-to-end fine-tuning.
watch_item: The guarantees require the stated convexity, quadratic-coupling, and quadratic-growth assumptions and are fixed-horizon rather than unrestricted convergence guarantees.
paper_title: Learning inexact alternating minimization for convex problems with quadratic coupling
